body.statement: There is an interval specified by \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\). The guarantee uses only the observed sample, the known values \(M\), \(\epsilon\), and \(\alpha\), and the conditions defining \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).
body.justification: The corrected handle exposes the intended sample split and all-heavy identity but does not claim unproved radii.
body.gap: Both the selected-factorial light radius and the winsorized Gaussian/fallback heavy radius lack explicit valid sample maps and tail theorems.
body.consumer: The intended consumer is a uniformly valid replacement for the reference intervals in the Zeng et al. 401(k) analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: Finite-sample coverage and the sharp expected-radius bound for an explicit heavy-light interval on the unrestricted global class.
obligation.obstruction: The rare radius remains unresolved, and the heavy winsorized self-normalized Gaussian/fallback score is still not an explicit sample map. The exact all-heavy center/variance override does not itself furnish a confidence radius.
obligation.attempted: The error was decomposed into deterministic light bias, light fluctuation, heavy fluctuation and truncation, and pilot terms. Only the banked light bias and the local all-heavy event close from the current primitives.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved node \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\) supplies the
deterministic light-branch bias allowance
\(C_\epsilon Md/[n\log(en)]\).  The corrected heavy-light handle now exposes
the pilot threshold and the exact all-heavy center/variance override, but it
deliberately leaves both radii as proposed outputs.  If measurable light and
heavy radii obeyed, on a common pilot-good event,
\[
 Q_P\{|T_{\mathrm L}-E(T_{\mathrm L}\mid I_0)|>R_{\mathrm L}\mid I_0\}
 \le\alpha/4,
 \qquad
 Q_P\{|T_{\mathrm H}-E(T_{\mathrm H}\mid I_0)|>R_{\mathrm H}\mid I_0\}
 \le\alpha/2,
\]
had expected radii of orders
\(M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\) and \(Mn^{-1/2}\), and the pilot-dependent
conditional means and failure event were controlled at the remaining level,
then the triangle inequality and a union bound would give coverage
\(1-\alpha\).  Clipping to \([-2M,2M]\) would not enlarge length.  None of
these radius hypotheses is yet a proved property of an explicit sample map.
